extracted.intended_audience: SEC registrants (public companies), corporate counsel, auditors, and other preparers of SEC financial disclosures
extracted.subtask_description: Interpreting and implementing the SEC's final climate-related disclosure and related Regulation S-X/S-K rules, including scope, safe-harbors, presentation and attribution requirements for financial statement effects of climate risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forward-looking statement classification (Item 1504)
rubrics_metrics.description: A projection or estimate of a registrant's future GHG emissions made pursuant to Item 1504 would likely constitute a forward-looking statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statements that are projections or estimates of future metrics (for example future GHG emissions) should be evaluated as forward-looking statements and thus may implicate statutory safe harbors (e.g., PSLRA safe harbors) and other doctrines depending on the facts and circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other safe harbors and doctrines may apply
rubrics_metrics.description: Other safe harbors, such as Securities Act Rule 175 and Exchange Act Rule 3b-6 and the bespeaks caution doctrine may also continue to apply to disclosures made pursuant to any of the subpart 1500 provisions, depending on specific facts and circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing liability exposure for climate-related disclosures, consider whether Rule 175, Rule 3b-6, or the bespeaks caution doctrine could apply in addition to PSLRA protections; applicability is fact-specific.

rubrics_metrics.name: PSLRA safe harbor exceptions (IPO and certain offerings)
rubrics_metrics.description: The PSLRA safe harbors do not apply to statements made in connection with an IPO, or made in connection with an offering by, or related to the operations of, a partnership, limited liability company, or a direct participation investment program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare climate-related forward-looking disclosures with the understanding that PSLRA protections are limited in these contexts (see 15 U.S.C. 77z-2(b)(2)(D)/(E) and 78u-5(b)(2)(D)/(E)).

rubrics_metrics.name: PSLRA safe harbor scope as to who is covered
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to issuers, consistent with the PSLRA safe harbors, the safe harbor will apply to: a person acting on behalf of the issuer; an outside reviewer retained by the issuer making a statement on behalf of the issuer; or an underwriter, with respect to information provided by the issuer or information derived from information provided by the issuer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entities and persons who make statements on behalf of the issuer or that rely on issuer-provided information may be covered by the safe harbor; disclose and document the provenance of information accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'blank check company' (for Sec. 27A/21E)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission recently amended Securities Act Rule 405 and Exchange Act Rule 12b-2 to define 'blank check company' for purposes of Securities Act Section 27A and Exchange Act Section 21E to mean a company that has no specific business plan or purpose or has indicated that its business plan is to engage in a merger or acquisition with an unidentified company or companies, or other entity or person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify registrants consistent with the amended definition when determining applicability of certain safe-harbor exclusions and other tailored rules for blank check companies (e.g., SPACs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Final rules limited to presentation and disclosure (not recognition/measurement)
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules establish presentation and disclosure requirements; they do not alter or establish recognition and measurement requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementers should treat the rules as prescribing how climate-related impacts are presented/disclosed in financial statements and notes, while recognition and measurement (GAAP) remain subject to existing accounting standards and FASB guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization of Regulation S-X amendments as financial statement effects disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules do not use the term 'metrics' to describe the Regulation S-X amendments because the Commission thinks it is more accurate to characterize them as disclosures of financial statement effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing required items under Regulation S-X, frame required amounts as effects on financial statements (capitalized costs, expenditures expensed, charges, losses) rather than standalone 'metrics.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of where impacts are presented in financial statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement to disclose where on the balance sheet and income statement the required capitalized costs, expenditures expensed, charges, and losses are presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each disclosed capitalized cost, expensed expenditure, charge, or loss attributable to climate-related events or activities, identify the specific financial statement line item(s) and note location where those amounts are presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle for attributing expenditures to severe weather or natural conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopting a principle for attributing an expenditure to a severe weather event or other natural condition and for determining the amount to be disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrants must apply the Commission's adopted attribution principle to determine which expenditures are attributable to a specified severe weather event or natural condition and calculate the amount to disclose; see section II.K.3.c.iii for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to determine impacts on each consolidated financial statement line item
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant would be required to determine the impacts of severe weather events, other natural conditions, transition activities, and identified climate-related risks on each consolidated financial statement line item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess and quantify how identified climate-related risks and activities affect each consolidated-line item (balance sheet and income statement) to inform the Regulation S-X disclosures of financial statement effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure threshold requirement for financial statement effects
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a disclosure threshold requirement (see discussion in section II.K.3.c.ii) that governs when the financial statement effects must be disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the specified threshold test before preparing line-item effect disclosures; details on the threshold and its application are discussed in the referenced section of the release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope/applicability to interim and Form 10-Q filings
rubrics_metrics.description: The note to the financial statements will not be required in a Form 10-Q filing. Similarly, the note to the financial statements will not be required for unaudited interim financial statements included in a registration statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include the full financial-statement-note style disclosure in Form 10-Q or unaudited interim registration-statement financial statements where the rule exempts it; ensure compliance with applicable scope limits and cross-check other disclosure obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: MD&A (Item 303) cross-obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants are reminded that they may nonetheless have an obligation to discuss climate-related information in MD&A if the information meets the requirements for disclosure under Item 303 of Regulation S-K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if specific Regulation S-X line-item disclosures are not triggered, evaluate Item 303 (Management's Discussion & Analysis) obligations and disclose climate information there if material under Item 303 standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminology: 'charges' and 'losses' reflect prior proposed metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: While the final rules use the terms 'charges' and 'losses' in the disclosure requirements related to expenditures, these terms represent impacts that would have been disclosed under the proposed Financial Impact Metrics and, accordingly, the Commission does not consider these to be an expansion of the proposed disclosure requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When mapping prior proposed metric line items to final-rule disclosure items, treat 'charges' and 'losses' as representing the same types of financial impacts previously contemplated under Financial Impact/Expenditure metric proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance of disaggregated disclosure (analogy to segment and revenue disaggregation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission notes the importance of disaggregated disclosure (e.g., segment reporting, ASC Topic 280 and ASC 606/IFRS 15 revenue disaggregation) and analogizes the need for disaggregation in climate-related financial effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide disaggregated information where appropriate so users can understand how nature, amount, timing, and uncertainty of cash flows and financial positions are affected by climate factors; consider segment-like or category disaggregation consistent with existing reporting frameworks where feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overlap risk between Financial Impact and Expenditure disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters noted and the Commission acknowledged that the Financial Impact Metrics and Expenditure Metrics, as proposed, potentially would result in some overlapping disclosures with respect to costs and expenditures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing disclosures, identify and avoid double-counting by understanding how amounts reported under different disclosure buckets relate and by applying the Commission's attribution and mapping guidance (see discussion of overlap and mapping in the release).

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission retains authority regarding accounting presentation/form
rubrics_metrics.description: The securities laws provide the Commission authority to prescribe the form or forms in which required information shall be set forth, the items or details to be shown in financial statements, and the methods to be followed in preparation of accounts; SEC rules and releases are sources of authoritative GAAP for registrants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that while FASB is a designated standard setter, the Commission may prescribe presentation/disclosure form and incorporate or reference FASB guidance; coordinate disclosure and presentation choices with accounting advisors and auditors.
